## cf09cffb4663

**Concrete issue: the generated curriculum supports an exact-component-size shortcut that the canonical task refutes.**

Plausible rival:

> Recolor a blue cell red only when it is the center of an isolated four-connected component consisting of exactly five cells in a unit plus.

The generator places only separated unit pluses, so every blue component has exactly five cells. Across 120 generated draws (40 per difficulty band), this rival matched the intended output 120/120 times, and no draw contained a non-five-cell blue component.

Exact canonical counterexample input:

```text
000000000
000010000
000010000
001111100
000010000
000010000
011100000
000000000
000000000
```

The intended rule changes zero-based cell `(3,4)` from blue `1` to red `2`, because its four cardinal neighbors are blue. Its connected component is larger than five cells, so the rival changes nothing. The published output and intended local-neighborhood rule agree; the rival does not.

There is also a validator defect: `self_check([[9]])` returns `[]`. The branch that detects colors outside `(0,1)` returns the still-empty `errs` list. Thus wrong in-range ARC colors are silently accepted.

Recommended generator repair: include canonical-like crosses embedded in longer lines and mixed component sizes, declare the exact-five-component rival, and make `self_check` append a palette error instead of returning an empty list. Evidence: `checks/audit-cf-shortcut-probe.log`.
